messages:
maria: Quick sync — I pushed profiling from the last 24h run. Seeing repeated 1-2s stalls when microbursts hit and kernels switch mid-batch.

sam: link?

maria: https://internal.perf/reports/2069/burst-run (perf summary in the doc). Key bit: KV cache hit rate drops ~18% during burst windows, and kernel latency variance spikes.

ryan: hmm that aligns with what I saw — batch assembler creates tiny batches then concat causes kernel mismatch. We end up switching from fused-attn -> baseline which costs 400ms.

anya: are we sure it's kernel selection and not memory thrash? any OOMs?

maria: no OOM. P99 mem ok. Kernel flip is triggered by effective sequence-length estimate when partial batches are NaN-ish because KV hits change.

sam: sketch of a mitigation: add a short coalescing window (3-8ms) that will delay admit for tiny requests during burst, plus a soft-reject path that returns 429 with Retry-After when token_budget <= X. That should avoid flipping kernels mid-batch.

ryan: agree on coalescing window. Also propose token_budget smoothing: keep moving-average of budget over 200ms and only soft-reject when MA < threshold. avoids oscillation.

anya: any cost in added latency for small requests? microrequests from UI expect <100ms. 5ms coalesce might be acceptable, but need to quantify tail.

maria: quick numbers from simulator: 5ms window reduces kernel flips by ~72% and increases median latency for 1-3 token requests by 4ms. p99 improves by ~200ms.

sam: sounds promising. We should also prefer kernel pinning if batch composition is heterogeneous: if >60% of tokens in batch favor fused kernel, keep fused for the batch and spill smaller ones to fallback queue.

ryan: implementable: add batch-level kernel-tag and fallback queue classification. Fallback queue will be lower priority and get admitted only when capacity.

anya: how about KV cache interaction — simulator assumes independent hits, but real trace shows hit correlation across bursts. any plan to keep KV availability stable?

maria: plan: when we detect a burst, be conservative with KV-ejection; lower eviction aggressiveness by 30% for 500ms window to maintain hits. That keeps hit rate and reduces rewarm cost.

sam: we should harden soft-429 semantics: return a machine-readable body with suggested retry-ms and a metric-tag so Console can aggregate. e.g., {"code":"soft_429","retry_ms":120,"policy":"coalesce-v1"} 

anya: +1. Also add a new metric to trace: admit_path=(coalesced|direct|soft-reject) and kernel_selected=(fused|baseline|padded).

maria: here's the proposed experiment plan:
- rollout coalescer on 10% nodes for 6h ramp
- enable token_budget smoothing window=200ms, ma_threshold=0.15 (15% of token budget)
- eviction_aggressiveness *= 0.7 for burst windows
- enable soft-429 with retry_ms=120 on coalesced nodes
- collect p50/p95/p99 latency, kernel_flip_rate, kv_hit_rate, soft_429_rate

ryan: add a canary synthetic workload (mixed short/long seqs with burst injection) to the CI perf job so we can automatically compare before/after. ci-bot: can you create the perf job?

ci-bot: created perf job "burst-coalescer-canary" and queued the synthetic test. Results will appear in ~2h.

sam: data collection note: correlate user token_cost metric to ensure we don't regress cost-per-token due to padding. Need a guard: if avg token-per-inference rises >5% on canary, rollback.

anya: eco check: does coalescing hurt throughput for sustained loads? it might add jitter. Need sustained-load test too.

maria: yep we'll run both sustained and burst canaries. If sustained throughput drops >3% we abort.

ryan: implementation tasks: (1) Admit coalescer in queue manager (2) MA token budget smoothing (3) batch kernel-tagging + fallback queue (4) eviction tweak + metrics + soft-429 body. I'll split PRs.

sam: timeline?

ryan: pick up (1)+(2) today, aim for PRs by EOD tomorrow. (3)+(4) in follow-up.

maria: thanks all — tagging prod-oncall for awareness: @anya please escalate if soft-429s spike during ramp.

anya: will monitor dashboards and add alert: soft_429_rate > 0.5% sustained -> page.

sam: one more thought: if kernel flip source is stale sequence_length estimate because of incomplete KV metadata, maybe we can annotate requests with expected-kernel hint from client when applicable. long-term, but worth noting.

maria: noted. For now let's proceed with coalescer + smoothing experiment. I'll update the doc with exact metric queries and perf links.

ryan: great. CI job queued, will watch.

ci-bot: perf results: synthetic canary finished. Summary: kernel_flip_rate -72%, p99 latency -190ms, soft_429_rate 0.12%, avg tokens/inference +0.8%.

maria: looks good — merging canary to 30% next if no surprises.
